main-directive.mission: Convert SaborEspecial from a single-tenant-deployed app wearing a multi-tenant schema into a true runtime multi-tenant SaaS, while paying down the build, asset, and duplication debt that will compound linearly with every new cafeteria onboarded.
main-directive.business-premise: The product is SaaS for cafeterias. Revenue scales with tenant count. Therefore: adding tenant N+1 must cost one row insert, not one deploy. Every architectural decision in this sprint is evaluated against that single sentence.

non-negotiables.item: Zero cross-tenant data leakage. Enforced at DB, API, and cache layers.
No regression to existing tenant's UX during migration. Feature-flag every cutover.
Every change ships behind CI gates: tests pass, bundle budget holds, lint clean.
No new dependencies without written justification against existing stack.
Observability before optimization. If we can't measure it, we don't ship it.

engineering-principles.principle: Tenant identity is resolved once per request, in one place, and passed as immutable context. No re-derivation downstream.
Absence of a tenant context is an error, never a default. Missing RLS policy denies access, never permits.
Shared logic lives in /shared or /lib. Re-implementation in a page-level script is a code-review block, not a style preference.

principle.name: Cache What Is Versioned, Network What Is Live

engineering-principles.principle: Hashed assets are immutable and cache-first. API responses are network-first with explicit TTL on snapshots.
Deploying twice with no code change must produce no client-visible churn. SW cache versions are derived, not hand-bumped.
We don't introduce a framework, ORM, or service mesh in this sprint. We sharpen what exists.

success-metrics.metric: Of API requests carry a resolved tenant_id in middleware-attached context.
Of tenant-scoped tables enforce RLS policies pinned to JWT claim.
Total critical-path JS + CSS per first paint.
Duplicate implementations of any helper detected by jscpd.
Cost to onboard tenant N+1, end-to-end.

phasing.phase: WS-01, WS-02, WS-03 — multi-tenant runtime is unblockable prerequisite.
WS-04, WS-05, WS-06, WS-07 — parallelizable after WS-01 lands.
WS-08, WS-09 — locks in the gains; prevents regression.

workstream.title: Runtime Tenant Resolution
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: this is the load-bearing decision of the sprint. Touches request lifecycle, auth, session, and every downstream API. Must be owned by the engineer with the deepest knowledge of the request boundary.
workstream.objective: Establish a single, authoritative function that resolves the active cafeteria_id for every inbound request, exposes it as immutable context, and removes all per-deploy tenant configuration.

requirements.requirement: Implement lib/tenant-context.js exporting resolveTenant(req). Resolution precedence: (1) JWT claim cafeteria_id, (2) subdomain ({slug}.saborespecial.app), (3) path segment (/s/{slug}). Returns { id, slug, plan, features } or throws TenantNotResolved.
Replace every direct cafeteria_id read in api/*.js with the resolved context. No handler is permitted to accept cafeteria_id from the request body.

Add endpoint GET /api/tenant-config returning the public per-tenant config (branding tokens, feature flags, payment provider key). Replaces the static /config.js pattern referenced by every HTML page.
Remove the per-deploy slug rewrite in vercel.json. One deployment serves all tenants.
Emit structured log line tenant.resolved with tenant_id, source (jwt|subdomain|path), and request_id for every request. Feeds SM-1.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: 100% of /api/* handlers receive tenant via context, verified by static grep test in CI.
Onboarding tenant #2 in staging requires only a row insert into cafeterias + DNS — no deploy.
Request with no resolvable tenant returns HTTP 400 with code TENANT_UNRESOLVED, never falls through to a default.
Load test: 1k req/s mixed across 3 tenants shows zero context leakage in logs.

workstream.dependencies: None. Unblocks WS-02, WS-03, WS-07, WS-08.
workstream.rollback: Feature flag TENANT_RUNTIME_RESOLVE. If off, system reverts to legacy per-deploy slug path. Flag burns down after WS-09 closes.

workstream.title: Postgres Row-Level Security Audit & Enforcement
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: RLS is the last line of defense against cross-tenant leakage. Must be owned by the engineer with deepest SQL and Supabase auth-chain expertise.
workstream.objective: Every tenant-scoped table denies access by default and permits only rows matching the cafeteria_id claim in the authenticated JWT.

requirements.requirement: Inventory every table in supabase/migrations/*.sql. Classify as tenant-scoped, global, or system. Output: docs/RLS_INVENTORY.md.
For each tenant-scoped table, add migration enabling RLS and policies: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE each gated on cafeteria_id = (auth.jwt() ->> 'cafeteria_id')::uuid.
Add negative tests in scripts/test-integrity.js: tenant A JWT cannot read/write tenant B rows. One test per tenant-scoped table.
Audit the 7 analytics views in supabase/migrations/004_analytics_views.sql. Confirm views inherit RLS from underlying tables or recreate with explicit WHERE cafeteria_id = ....
Document the service-role escape hatch: which scripts use it, why, and the audit log expected. No service-role usage outside documented list.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Every tenant-scoped table reports rowsecurity = true in pg_tables.
Cross-tenant negative tests pass for 100% of tenant-scoped tables.
Service-role usage outside the documented list fails CI.

workstream.rollback: Migrations are forward-only with explicit down scripts. RLS can be disabled per-table via emergency migration if production incident occurs; requires CTO approval.

workstream.title: Tenant-Aware Service Worker & Per-Tenant Config Loading
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: SW cache contamination across tenants is a correctness bug, not a perf nit. Requires deep SW lifecycle knowledge.
workstream.objective: Service Worker caches partition by tenant; per-tenant config loads at runtime from the API, never from a static /config.js.

requirements.requirement: Modify sw.js cache names to include tenant slug: se-app-${slug}-v${hash}. Resolution at SW install via self.registration.scope + posted message from page on activation.
Replace static /config.js includes across all 7 HTML files with a runtime fetch of /api/tenant-config on app boot. Cached in sessionStorage with 15-min TTL keyed by tenant slug.
On tenant switch (e.g., logout / re-login as different cafeteria user), call caches.delete() for all non-matching cache keys.
Add SW integration test: simulate two tenants on same browser; assert tenant A's cached menu is never served to tenant B.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Cache keys in DevTools Application panel are tenant-prefixed.
No HTML file references /config.js as a static asset.
Cross-tenant cache leakage test passes.

workstream.rollback: SW version bump invalidates all caches client-side; safe to revert without server change.

workstream.title: Build Pipeline — esbuild, Compression, Fingerprinting
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: this is the asset-pipeline foundation. Every other perf win compounds on top of it. Wrong choice here costs the team for years.
workstream.objective: All client-shipped JS and CSS are minified, gzipped/brotli-served, content-hashed, and aggressively cached. Build is < 5 seconds cold, < 1 second warm.

requirements.requirement: Add esbuild as devDependency. Config in scripts/build.mjs. Inputs: app.js, management.js, deliveries.js, track.js, login.js, signup.js, customer-app.html entry. Outputs: dist/*.[hash].js, dist/*.[hash].css.
Add vercel.json headers config: Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on /dist/*; Cache-Control: no-cache on *.html.
Enable compression at the platform layer (Vercel ships brotli by default; verify response headers in staging).
Generate dist/manifest.json mapping logical name → hashed filename. HTML templating layer (WS-08) consumes it.
Emit build report: per-bundle size, gzip size, delta vs baseline. Written to dist/build-report.json for CI consumption.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Critical-path JS+CSS < 60 KB gzipped (SM-3).
SW cache version derives from build manifest hash, not hand-edited (closes EP-5).
Cold build < 5s on CI runner.
Lighthouse performance score >= 90 on staging.

workstream.dependencies: None. Can run parallel to WS-01/02/03.
workstream.rollback: Vercel rollback to prior deploy reverts asset paths. Old SW cache versions remain valid until expiry.

workstream.title: Service Worker Strategy — Cache-First for App Shell

assigned-engineer.role: Senior Frontend / PWA Engineer (continues from WS-03)

workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: same engineer owns SW lifecycle end-to-end. Avoids ownership fragmentation.
workstream.objective: Hashed app-shell assets serve cache-first, eliminating ~200 ms network round-trip on repeat visits. API requests remain network-first with cache fallback.

requirements.requirement: In sw.js, classify requests: (a) hashed asset under /dist/* → cache-first, (b) /api/* GET → network-first with cache fallback, (c) HTML → network-first.
On activation, prune caches not matching current build hash. No more manual v13 bumps.
Add explicit TTL (15 min) to cached /api/* responses; expired entries trigger network refetch even on cache hit.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Repeat-visit TTI < 200 ms (SM-4) measured via Lighthouse on staging.
SW cache version no longer hand-edited; sourced from build manifest.

workstream.rollback: Revert sw.js commit; clients re-fetch on next activation.

workstream.title: Shared Utility Extraction — Kill Duplicate Implementations
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: surgical refactor across page-level scripts. Owner must be fluent in the existing DOM-direct codebase.
workstream.objective: Three functions, three locations, one canonical implementation each. Page scripts import from shared/; no inline re-implementations survive.

requirements.requirement: Move todayKey() to shared/formatters.js. Delete duplicates at app.js:58, management.js:124, management.js:1038 (inline). Reuse server-side lib/dashboard.js:28 definition where applicable.

Move setFeedback() to shared/ui-feedback.js. Delete duplicates at app.js:76, management.js:183, deliveries.js:63. Single signature: setFeedback(el, msg, level) where level ∈ {'info','success','error'}; colors sourced from CSS custom properties.
Move formatDateLabel() to shared/formatters.js. Delete duplicate at management.js:129. Align with lib/dashboard.js:90 formatTimestamp.
Add jscpd to CI (WS-09) configured to fail on any new duplicate > 5 lines across app.js, management.js, deliveries.js.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: jscpd reports zero duplicates among the three named functions.
No behavioral regression in existing integrity tests.

workstream.dependencies: WS-04 (so shared modules ship through the build pipeline).
workstream.rollback: Pure refactor behind unchanged public behavior; revertible by single commit.

workstream.title: API Consolidation — Merge /menu and /dashboard
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: API contract owner. Must coordinate breaking change with frontend consumers in management.js.
workstream.objective: One endpoint serves the overlapping read surface; query parameter controls included resources. Reduces handler code and eliminates duplicated Supabase query orchestration.

requirements.requirement: Introduce GET /api/dashboard?include=settings,menu,orders,stats. Default include list preserves current /api/dashboard behavior.
Delete api/menu.js after one-deploy deprecation window. Update all callers in management.js:797, :810, :830.
Document the new endpoint in docs/API.md (create if absent). Include tenant-context requirement from WS-01.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Single endpoint serves both prior call sites.
API surface line count drops by >= 40 lines net.
No frontend call site references /api/menu.

workstream.rollback: Re-enable api/menu.js handler from git; deprecation window prevents hard break.

workstream.title: HTML Templating & Per-Tenant Branding Slot
workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: spans server-rendered partials and client-side injection. Must understand both halves of the request.
workstream.objective: Remove ~420 lines of duplicated HTML across 7 files. Provide a single header/nav/footer partial that injects tenant branding (logo, name, theme tokens) at render time.

requirements.requirement: Introduce minimal template system: scripts/build.mjs processes {page}.template.html + partials in partials/{header,nav,footer}.html → emits final HTML to dist/. No runtime templating framework.
Branding slot: <meta name="tenant-bootstrap" data-endpoint="/api/tenant-config">. Client hydrates header logo/name/theme on boot from response.
Delete duplicated header/nav/footer markup from index.html, customer-app.html, management.html, deliveries.html, track.html, signup.html, and login.html.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Total HTML LOC drops by >= 400 lines.
Visual regression suite (one screenshot per page per tenant) shows zero unintended diffs.
Tenant branding visibly differs between two test tenants on staging.

workstream.rollback: Original HTML files preserved in git; build step can be disabled via env flag, falling back to static files.

workstream.title: CI/CD Gates — Bundle Budget, Lint, jscpd, Per-Tenant Smoke

assigned-engineer.role: Principal DevOps Engineer + Senior QA Engineer

workstream.assigned-engineer: Rationale: this workstream locks in every other workstream's gains. Without it, all wins regress within two sprints.
workstream.objective: Every PR is automatically blocked from introducing: (a) bundle growth, (b) lint violations, (c) code duplication, (d) cross-tenant regressions.

requirements.requirement: ESLint configured for the codebase. Rules: no-unused-vars, no-implicit-globals, prefer-const, eqeqeq. PR fails on any violation in changed files.
jscpd configured with threshold: zero duplicates > 5 lines across all *.js in repo root and shared/.
Bundle-budget check: compare dist/build-report.json (from WS-04) against .bundle-baseline.json. Fail PR if any bundle grows > 5% over baseline. Baseline updated only via explicit commit.
Pre-commit hook (husky or equivalent): run ESLint + jscpd on staged files. Fast path only; full CI runs the heavy suite.
Add .github/workflows/perf.yml: Lighthouse CI on every preview deploy. Threshold: performance >= 85.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: PR introducing a 10 KB bundle bump is blocked by CI.
PR introducing a duplicate todayKey() is blocked by jscpd.
PR breaking RLS isolation is blocked by per-tenant smoke.

workstream.dependencies: WS-01 (tenant context), WS-02 (RLS), WS-04 (build report), WS-06 (shared modules).
workstream.rollback: CI gates can be disabled per-workflow via repo settings if an emergency hotfix is required; logged and reviewed weekly.

wave.note: WS-01 is the critical path. WS-04 runs parallel because it has zero dependencies on tenant work and unblocks WS-05/06/08.

risk.description: Cross-tenant data leak during WS-01 rollout.
risk.mitigation: Feature flag TENANT_RUNTIME_RESOLVE; canary one staging tenant for 48h before prod; WS-02 RLS lands within same sprint to provide defense in depth.

risk.description: RLS policies break existing service-role scripts (migrate, seed, accounting export).
risk.mitigation: WS-02 R-02-5 mandates explicit service-role inventory. Tests run before policies merge.

risk.description: Build pipeline breaks existing deploy contract; assets 404 in prod.
risk.mitigation: WS-04 ships with parallel-path deploy: hashed assets live alongside legacy paths for one deploy cycle; cutover after smoke passes.

risk.description: HTML templating (WS-08) introduces visual regressions across 7 pages.
risk.mitigation: Screenshot diff suite required as acceptance criterion. PR blocked on visual delta > 2%.
WS-09 jscpd gate enforced at PR boundary; pre-commit hook catches at developer machine.

exit-criteria.criterion: 100% of API requests carry resolved tenant context.
Critical-path JS+CSS < 60 KB gzipped on prod.
jscpd reports zero duplicates of named helpers.
Onboarding tenant N+1 demonstrated end-to-end via single SQL insert + DNS entry.
All CI gates from WS-09 enforced on main branch.
All feature flags introduced during sprint are either burned down or scheduled for burndown next sprint.
